doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The NEA Jazz Master award, city honors and doctorates
summary: Antoinette Handy called her about the $20,000 award; she values her doctorates above Dorothy Donegan Day and keys to the city.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: American Jazz Master Award from the National Endowment for the Arts, 1992. An honor for you? You’re smiling, tell me about that.
Somebody called me up, Antoinette Handy, called me up and she said, “I been looking for you for four weeks.” So I said, “Do I owe you money?” She said, “No, I have
something to give you.” I started crying. She said, “We got $20,000 for you.” I said, “Ohhhh, Ohhh.” She said, “It’s true.” So, that’s how I got that.
You mentioned honorary doctorates. What other awards and honors have you received? I remember Dorothy Donegan Day, your birthday, I think 1974 in Chicago, keys to the City, that type of thing.
Oh yeah, I get that in New Orleans and Chicago, too.
What awards have you received that you’re most proud of?
The doctorates. I like those better. When they gave me one, I said, “Ohhhhh.” I started crying. I said, “My husbands call me more than that.”
